newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares seen calmer after turbulent Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares seen calmer after turbulent Tuesday.

text.p: Belgian shares were seen calmer in the days ahead after a roller coaster session on Tuesday marked the end of an equally turbulent two week account, dealers said.

Although there was still a lot of cash looking for a home, the July 1-2 meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy making committee could keep investors sidelined. A new account usually draws buyers into the market.
"There's cash out there, I'm just not sure if it will be dumped on the market at unreasonable prices," one trader said. "Most of the flows seem to be foreign, not domestic."

The Bel-20 blue chip index ended the day 3.57 points, or 0.15 percent, higher at 2,355.19 points, after moving in a 35 point range during the day in active dealings worth some 5.5 billion Belgian francs.
Tuesday's close compared with 2,352.13 points at the start of the account on June 11 and the new record high of 2,410.80 set on June 13.

Dealers did not expect the high to be retested this week, even if Wall Street continued to rally from its 2.5 percent loss on Monday. "What we saw today was Europe largely ignoring New York," one said. The Dow was up 0.50 pct by the Brussels close.
Tuesday's heaviest traded stocks included oil group PetroFina, up 250 francs, or 1.9 percent, at 13,225 francs in a large volume of 46,095 shares.
One senior trader said he was not aware of any reason for the renewed interest.
PetroFina is presently awaiting SEC approval for a September listing in New York and has made a friendly cash offer to buy out the minorities of its U.S. Fina Inc unit.
Utility group Tractebel was also heavily traded, with a block of 26,000 shares at 15,000 francs crossing the market, but ended down 50 francs at 14,900 francs.

Retailer Delhaize was active on news of expansion into Asia, a new market for the company. Delhaize announced earlier it would start a supermarket venture in Indonesia to add to a Thai venture announced on Monday.
The news was applauded by investors, who pushed Delhaize's share up 20 francs to 1,880 francs.
Bank Dexia CC edged ahead five francs to 3,895 francs ahead of the payment of an 87.75 franc net dividend on Wednesday.
Additional Dexia CC shares are due to be listed on Thursday, following on from a secondary offering made by its publicly-owned controlling shareholder.
